chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And upon those who are able [to fast, but do so] is a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [for each day],' he said: 'Those who were able to tolerate the fasting, but old age has hit them, or thirst, or something resembling that, so upon them, for each day, is a handful (of food to be fed to the poor).'

key_terms.طَعامُ مِسْكِينٍ: Food of a poor person: The specific form of compensation required
key_terms.عُطَاشٌ: Utash: Thirst or chronic condition causing thirst
key_terms.فِدْيَةٌ: Fidyah: Compensation or ransom paid by those unable to fast
key_terms.مُدٌّ: Mudd: A specific measure of volume, described here as a handful
key_terms.يُطِيقُونَهُ: Yutiqunahu: Those who are able to endure (the hardship of fasting but find it difficult)

ai.seo_question: What is the fidyah (compensation) for those who cannot fast due to old age or illness?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the exegetical meaning of 'those who can exert [effort]' in Quran 2:184, identifying them as the elderly or chronically ill who lack the capacity to fast. It establishes the specific legal ruling that their compensation is feeding one poor person per missed day, quantified as a 'mudd' of food, thereby grounding the practical application of fidyah in the Prophet's household tradition.
